newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Van den Broek sees U.S. as Turkey-Greece mediator.
newsitem.headline: Van den Broek sees U.S. as Turkey-Greece mediator.

text.p: EU Foreign Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek said on Wednesday the United States could most easily take the lead in fostering better relations between antagonistic neighbours Greece and Turkey.

"I'm inclined to say an appeal should be made to the United States, where relations between Greece and Turkey are concerned, to help bring the two sides closer together," he said at a lunch meeting with journalists in The Hague.
Van den Broek said the European Union would have to pay considerable attention to its relations with Turkey and to the situation in the divided island of Cyprus this year.

Tensions between Greece -- an EU member -- and Turkey have flared up recently over Cyprus government plans to buy surface-to-air missiles and Turkish threats to take action to prevent their deployment.
Van den Broek said the EU was prepared to take a leading role alongside the United Nations in finding a solution to the Cyprus problem.
But the United States was better placed to mediate between Greece and Turkey, he said, because Turkey had long viewed EU member states as allies of Greece.

"The Turks have always had a strong tendency to view the member states of the European Union as firm allies of Greece...That perception exists and that means the United States are in a better position," he said
Van den Broek said the EU faced a number of interlinked dilemmas concerning Cyprus and the poor relations between Greece and non-member Turkey.

He recalled that the EU had pledged to start membership negotiations with Cyprus no more than six months after conclusion of an inter-government conference on EU reform, adding that the EU should keep its word on this.
At the same time, Van den Broek said, recent tensions between Greece and Turkey would not make the Cyprus membership talks any easier.
The best way forward, he said, would be to make simultaneous progress on two fronts: addressing the political problems in Cyprus itself and reducing tensions between Greece and Turkey.
